title: Small-set expansion event bound
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $0$ and $1$, and suppose its uniform mean is $\alpha$. Draw $(X,Y)$ by choosing $X$ uniformly from the sign cube and then independently, in each coordinate, keeping its sign with probability $2/3$ and flipping it with probability $1/3$. Then $\mathbb P(f(X)=f(Y)=1)\le\alpha^{3/2}$.
replaced:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $0$ and $1$,
and let its uniform mean be $\alpha$. If $(X,Y)$ is drawn by choosing $X$ uniformly and
then independently flipping each coordinate of $X$ with probability $1/3$, then $\mathbb
P(f(X)=f(Y)=1)\leq \alpha^{3/2}$.
